I can’t export **root’s** crontab from here because this session doesn’t have elevated (sudo) exec enabled.

If you run this on the host, it will write root’s crontab to a temp file:

```sh
sudo crontab -l > /tmp/root-crontab.txt
ls -l /tmp/root-crontab.txt
```

If you want, enable elevated exec for webchat (`tools.elevated.enabled`) and I can do it directly.
[Sat 2026-05-09 07:24 UTC] Modify the temporary file to remove all scheduled command lines.

I can’t modify `/tmp/root-crontab.txt` from here because I don’t have elevated access to create/edit that root-owned temp file in this session.

On the host, this will remove all *scheduled* lines (leaving comments, blank lines, and environment/variable assignments) **in place**:

```sh
sudo sed -i.bak -E '/^[[:space:]]*(@(reboot|yearly|annually|monthly|weekly|daily|midnight|hourly)|([0-9*\/,-]+[[:space:]]+){4}[0-9*\/,-]+)[[:space:]]+/d' /tmp/root-crontab.txt
```

Optional: view result + backup:
```sh
sudo sed -n '1,200p' /tmp/root-crontab.txt
sudo ls -l /tmp/root-crontab.txt /tmp/root-crontab.txt.bak
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 07:25 UTC] Import the resulting empty file back into the root crontab configuration.

I can’t import into **root’s** crontab from here because elevated/sudo exec isn’t enabled in this session.

On the host, run:

```sh
sudo crontab /tmp/root-crontab.txt
sudo crontab -l
```

That will replace root’s crontab with the (now empty of scheduled jobs) contents of the temp file, then print it to verify.
